subject: Acme - Performance SLO/SLA follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>, Priya Rao <priya@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Acme - Performance SLO/SLA follow-up

Hi Jordan and Priya -

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap of what I heard and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

Summary of Acme requirements (as discussed):
- Latency: p95 <= 150ms for interactive text generation (expected median payload ~512 tokens). Streaming support required for first-token+streaming to UI.
- Throughput: sustained 1,000 requests/minute during business hours, occasional spikes up to 2,500 reqs/min.
- Concurrency: target ~100 concurrent sessions with per-session KV cache reuse.
- SLAs: monthly reporting, p95 and p99 latency SLIs, availability target 99.9% for hosted endpoints.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows, customer network issues, and misbehaving clients (we should clarify).

Next steps we agreed:
1) Redwood to propose SLO/SLA wording and measurement definition (we'll include how latency is measured and exclusions). Rishi will draft tech notes.
2) Acme to confirm expected payload sizes and percent streaming traffic to validate batching/throughput assumptions.
3) Exchange a draft SLA for legal review and attach examples of SLO calculations.

I'm looping Rishi (SE) and Neha (Sales Ops) for follow-up on the specifics. Rishi - can you attach a short draft of the SLA language and a sample SLO calculation matrix?

Jordan/Priya - any corrections to the bullets above? If not, I'll send a proposed SLA language by Monday and include a proposed reporting cadence.

Thanks -
Marissa

Subject: Re: Acme - Performance SLO/SLA follow-up

Thanks Marissa - that summary looks right. A couple of clarifications from our side that will drive SLA wording:

1) Latency definition: For our UI we need first-byte/first-token latency to be low. Practically we care about time-to-first-token (so that streaming starts quickly) and time-to-last-token for full responses. Our internal target is p95 time-to-first-token <= 150ms and p99 time-to-last-token <= 800ms for the 512-token average. Can you confirm Redwood can measure both and which one would be the SLI?

2) Throughput concurrency: The 1,000 reqs/min is our sustained average during peak hours; we plan for ~30% of calls to be streaming (progressive tokens). Concurrency spikes to 100 are expected during certain workflows.

3) Reporting cadence: Monthly SLA report is fine; for the pilot a weekly summary would be helpful.

4) Remedies: for now we expect a credit-based remedy tied to % of minutes below availability and separate credits for SLO breaches. Please propose language.

Finally - please include callouts for exclusions (maintenance, force majeure, customer-side connectivity) and whether cold-starts/warmed KV cache are treated as exclusions.

Jordan

Senior Product Manager, Acme Inc.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Acme - Performance SLO/SLA follow-up

Marissa / Jordan - attaching a draft SLA paragraph and a small CSV that shows example SLO calc rows. High level technical notes below:

- Measurement points: Redwood can measure latency at two points: (A) server ingress-to-first-token (recommended for UI streaming responsiveness) and (B) server ingress-to-last-token (end-to-end). Both are measured from the moment the request is accepted by the runtime until the first/last token is emitted.
- Suggested SLIs: p95(first-token) and p99(last-token). For initial contract propose: p95(first-token) <= 150ms, p99(last-token) <= 800ms. We can include p50/p90 for operational visibility in the report.
- Exclusions we recommend: scheduled maintenance (we propose a max 4-hours/month scheduled window), documented customer-side outages (e.g., customer network or CDN issues), and incidents caused by customer payloads that exceed agreed limits (e.g., >2,048 token context for this deal). Cold-starts: we do not recommend blanket exclusion for cold-start latency after warm-up; instead propose a stabilization window for new model deploys (e.g., first 30 minutes after model rollout excluded).
- Remedies: credit table can be structured as percentage credits of monthly invoice tied to minutes below availability and separate credits for SLO breaches. Example: if p95(first-token) falls below target for >5% of minutes in a month, 5% credit; >10% -> 10% credit; escalate per tier. We'll draft exact language.
- Streaming: streaming sessions count as a single request for availability math; latency SLI is measured to first-token and to last-token as separate SLIs. Throughput calculations should account for token-generation concurrency; we'll include recommended concurrency knobs (batch size limits, prefix caching).

Attached: redwood_draft_sla_v1.pdf (draft SLA wording), slo_calculation_examples.csv (SLO calc rows).

-- Rishi

Subject: Acme - Draft SLA language and reporting cadence (for review)

Jordan/Priya -

Attached is a short draft (redwood_draft_sla_v1.pdf) that incorporates the items we discussed and Rishi's technical notes. Key points in the draft:
- SLIs: p95(first-token) and p99(last-token) with proposed targets of 150ms and 800ms respectively.
- Measurement method: measured at server ingress to token emission; streaming first-token and last-token measured independently.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows (max 4 hours/month), customer-side outages, documented load exceeding agreed payload limits, and a 30-minute exclusion window after model deploys/rollouts.
- Reporting cadence: monthly SLA report (CSV + short summary). Pilot: weekly reports for first 60 days.
- Remedies: tiered credit table tied to % of minutes below target and separate credit for availability breaches.

Request: please review the attached and confirm whether wording on remedies and exclusions is acceptable or if you want specific thresholds adjusted. Once you confirm, we'll move this to legal for redlines.

Marissa
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>

Cc: Priya Rao <priya@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Acme - Draft SLA language and reporting cadence (for review)

Thanks Marissa and Rishi - the draft looks good overall. A few minor asks before we send to legal:

1) Please add explicit monthly reporting cadence line: "Monthly SLA report to be delivered by the 7th business day of the month, with data for the prior calendar month."
2) Remedies: can we add a sample credit calculation example in the doc (line item showing how a 5% credit is calculated)?
3) Exclusions: please explicitly call out "customer network/connectivity issues" and "third-party CDN outages" in the exclusions list.

If you can incorporate those three small edits I'll get this to our legal team for review. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Jordan
